newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Cable & Wireless in China talks -- HK Tel.
newsitem.headline: Cable & Wireless in China talks -- HK Tel.

text.p: Hong Kong Telecommunications Ltd said on Friday that Cable & Wireless Plc and the Chinese authorities are having discussions following the signing of a Memorandum of Understanding between them last October.

"The Hongkong Telecom Board this morning announced that it is aware that discussions have been taking place between Cable and Wireless Plc and the Chinese authorities, following a signing of a Memorandum of Understanding between these parties on 30 October, 1996 for future cooperation with the Chinese Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications," the company said in a statement to the stock exchange.
"We understand that these discussions are continuing but there is no certainty as to how and when these will be concluded or as to their effect in relation to Hongkong Telecom," it added.

At the time the MOU was signed, Cable & Wireless (C&W) said it was a broad framework for future cooperation between the British telecom giant and China's Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications (MPT).

Speculation that C&W would sell part of its approximately 59 percent interest in Hongkong Telecom to a Chinese entity has fuelled repeated rounds of buying interest in the Hong Kong-based company's shares.
Hongkong Telecom shares surged to an intra-day record high of HK$18.35 on Friday morning before retreating to HK$18.10, up HK$1.00, at the midday. close.
Market talk suggested the buyer would be China's MPT or China United Telecommunications Corp.
China Everbright Group's purchase of 7.74 percent of Hongkong Telecom from CITIC Pacific Ltd earlier this year was view by many as the first move by China to extend it infulence in the company.
China Everbright is directly under the supervision of China's State Council.
